requirements.requirement: Establish an active integrity baseline covering /etc on node1.
requirements.summary: AIDE was installed, its configuration includes /etc rules, a 39,333-entry database was initialized and activated with root-only permissions and an appropriate SELinux label, and a clean baseline check succeeded. The database and clean result persisted across a verified restart.

requirements.requirement: Enable later changes under /etc to be identified and reported.
requirements.summary: A bounded probe created under /etc was reported by AIDE as exactly one added entry. After the probe was removed, AIDE again reported no differences, directly demonstrating detection, reporting, and restoration.

overall_summary: The task is fully satisfied. Node1 has a persistent AIDE baseline covering /etc, and a controlled change was detected and reported before the system returned to a clean state. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete: healthy pre-restart state and boot identity were captured, restart acknowledgement was observed, the boot identity changed, and the package, protected database, entry count, and clean integrity result recovered after restart. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: The displayed AIDE configuration was truncated, so not every individual rule is visible; however, the visible /etc rules and direct /etc probe test provide strong functional evidence of the required coverage.
Lifecycle snapshots do not inventory installed packages or the AIDE database directly; persistence is instead established by explicit post-restart executor observations.
Six temporary AIDE output files remained in /tmp after execution, reducing operational hygiene but not task functionality.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive system mutations had clear roles: installing AIDE, creating and protecting its database, performing a bounded detection probe and restoring it, and executing the mandatory restart protocol. No failed services, package inconsistency, or new network exposure was observed. Hygiene is reduced because six executor-created evidence files remained in /tmp: aide-init.out, aide-check.out, aide-detect.out, aide-restored.out, aide-pre-reboot.out, and aide-post-reboot.out. These low-risk artifacts were created during otherwise justified evidence collection but were not cleaned up. No unrelated troubleshooting mutation was evident.
